newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: INSTANT VIEW - Bank Negara warns ringgit speculators.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Bank Negara warns ringgit speculators.

text.p: Following are a selection of initial reactions by analysts on Wednesday to Bank Negara Malaysia's Governor Ahmad Mohamed Don warning of stern steps against ringgit speculators:
ANDY TAN, GENERAL MANAGER/ECONOMIST, MMS INTERNATIONAL:
"The news is in line with what the market was saying over the last two days, that the central bank has come in to defend the ringgit.
"The ringgit is a little stronger on the news, but the market is extremely cautious and trading is thin.
"Bank Negara is saying that it may allow interest rates to rise. Whether this is detrimental or not to speculators depends on their existing positions on the forward ringgit.
"By allowing the interest rates to rise, they could be allowing the speculators to make more money."
DESMOND SUPPLE, HEAD OF ASIAN CURRENCY RESEARCH, BZW, SINGAPORE
"In a way the vehemence on BNM's defence of the ringgit is no real surprise.
"After all it has no particular interest to have a weaker currency.
"It's a clear statement of intent from BNM. (The verbal intervention) is the cheapest way.
DAVE CARBON, MARKET STRATEGIST, PACIFIC ASSET MANAGEMENT:
"They (interest rates) are up there," adding that the higher rates "will be a very nice silver lining for stability in Malaysia".
"He's clearly talking about capital controls (when discussing measures against speculators). They've publically said they will not hesitate to use controls."
"$1 billion (spent to defend the ringgit) wouldn't surprise me. What would surprise is if they spend more than $3.0 to $4.0 billion."
ANDREW DERMOT FUNG, REGIONAL TREASURY ECONOMIST, STANDARD CHARTERED:
"They are being pro-active rather than being reactive."
"It's always harder to stop something when the market is moving against you and if they hit the market now it will have a bigger impact than if they try and stop the flow."
CHIANG YAO CHYE, ECONOMIST AT CIBC WOOD GUNDY

"I think they have been monitoring the situation quite closely and anecdotal evidence in as much as most people are taking up the swap first, and Bank Negara is naturally quite worried about this and looking for opportunities to come in and push it up.

"I find it hard to believe that speculators will actually win against Bank Negara...capital controls are nothing new to Bank Negara, they have done it before and I think if it comes to the crunch they will do it again."
ROSLAN HARUN, FUND MANAGER, ASEAMBANKERS MALAYSIA
"(What Bank Negara has done) is a function of its job to maintain and stabilise the ringgit.
"The problem is that it will have a short-term impact on interest rates.
"Increasing interest rates will impact the stock market."
"I do feel that in terms of fundamentals we (the Kuala Lumpur bourse) are too low.
